extracted.intended_audience: general readers of literary biography and 19th‑century American literature; readers interested in Quaker history and religious oratory
extracted.subtask_description: Producing or assessing biographical sketches of religious figures—emphasizing life‑details, demonstrable ministerial labors, authenticity of primary sources, and the depiction of oratory and inward spiritual authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noteworthiness of life (method, practicality, sincerity, earnestness, pure piety)
rubrics_metrics.description: His whole life was a long religious missionary life of method, practicality, sincerity, earnestness, and pure piety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitman treats these moral and practical qualities as the core reasons a life merits recording even if it lacks literary, political, or inventive fame; such exemplars 'deserve to be recorded and kept up as a sample.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Measured dedication to ministry (travel, meetings, refusal of salary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete measures of ministerial dedication: extensive journeys and many meetings (e.g., 'I was from home on this journey four months and eleven days; rode about one thousand five hundred miles, and attended forty-nine particular meetings...'), and a practice of accepting no salary except transportation, food and shelter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use factual counts (miles ridden, meetings attended, duration of absence) and behavioral details (refusing money for preaching) as objective evidence of commitment and seriousness in a minister's life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of primary journals despite dryness
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader who feels interested must get—with all its dryness and mere dates, absence of emotionality or literary quality—the 'Journal of the Life and Religious Labours of Elias Hicks, written by himself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize original, primary writings even if they are 'dry' or lack literary flourish; primary journals provide indispensable source material for authentic biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extempore, natural preaching over intellectual argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Elias's oratory was 'not argumentative or intellectual, but so penetrating... different from anything in the books,' a 'pleading, tender, nearly agonizing conviction' that moved audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting religious speech, emphasize spontaneous, heartfelt, extempore elements rather than polished intellectual argument—show audience reaction (tears, silence) as evidence of effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnetism / the unnameable charismatic element in oratory
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an 'unnameable something behind oratory...a sympathetic germ, probably rapport...which no book, no rule, no statement has given or can give...launch'd out only by powerful human magnetism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and attempt to convey the intangible, personal charisma that makes certain speakers compelling; treat it as a real, if ineffable, factor that resists formalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue‑neutral accessibility of preaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Elias preaches anywhere—'no respect to buildings--private or public houses, school-rooms, barns, even theatres--anything that will accommodate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray ministers' reach and populism by noting the variety of venues they used; accessibility and disregard for genteel venues can be a mark of their practical missionary spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inward 'Light' as the authoritative standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'inward law and light' is the rule by which 'the true and saving knowledge of God can be obtain'd' and 'by this inward law and light, all will be either justified or condemn'd.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In describing Quaker belief and authenticity, foreground the primacy of inward conscience/light over external creeds, scriptures' literalism, or institutional doctrines; treat adherence to this inward standard as central to religious identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical delivery and vocal qualities as part of oratory
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical aspects: 'resonant, grave, melodious voice,' dramatic gestures (dashing down his broad-brim hat), occasional nasality and sing-song interrupted by natural tone; a 'tall, straight figure' and 'piercing eyes' contributed to presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete physical and vocal details (voice quality, gestures, posture, facial expression) to render a speaker's presence and convey how delivery contributes to persuasive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spiritual exegesis (interpret texts spiritually, not literally)
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms of scriptural texts 'are not to be taken in their literal meaning, but in their spiritual one,' interpreting prophetic images as spiritual exaltations rather than literal descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characterizing a preacher's theology, note hermeneutic stance—here a spiritual/allegorical reading of scripture—which shapes sermons and the audience's understanding of religious promises and prophecy.
